title: A synagogue built for a returning community
description: The synagogue’s own film about the Kadoorie Mekor Haim, finished in 1938 for descendants of Jews forced to convert in the 1490s. A family of Jewish bankers in Hong Kong helped pay for it. It is the largest synagogue in Iberia.

title: A sandwich buried under cheese and sauce
episode: Portugal's Most Iconic Sandwich Is Smothered In Cheese And Sauce
place: Café Santiago, Rua de Passos Manuel
description: The francesinha, or “little Frenchwoman,” is Porto’s own sandwich: layers of meat under melted cheese and a spiced beer and tomato sauce, said to be adapted from the croque-monsieur in the 1950s. Café Santiago is a famous home for it.

title: Why Porto’s people are called tripe-eaters
episode: Protecting a Portuguese Delicacy Made of Cow’s Stomach, Pig’s Ear and Cow’s Feet
description: Tripas à moda do Porto, a stew of tripe and white beans, and the guild that protects the recipe. Locals say Porto gave its meat to the fleet that sailed to take Ceuta in 1415 and kept only the offal, which is why people here are still called tripeiros.

title: Sardines canned by hand since 1920
episode: Why This Portuguese Sardine Cannery Swears By Its 100-Year-Old Method
description: Inside Pinhais, a cannery in Matosinhos, Porto’s fishing harbor, where workers still clean, fry, and pack sardines by hand. Dozens of canneries once lined this coast; Pinhais is one of the last still working.

title: A tea house set into the rocks
episode: Learning with Álvaro Siza - Boa Nova Tea House
place: Casa de Chá da Boa Nova, Leça da Palmeira
description: Architect Álvaro Siza’s tea house on the rocks at Leça da Palmeira, finished in 1963 when he was barely 30. Low concrete and timber rooms sit between the boulders so the sea fills every window. It is now a restaurant.

title: Housing that waited 30 years to be finished
episode: Portugal's Communist Housing Estate by Álvaro Siza
description: The Bouça estate, which Álvaro Siza began in the 1970s for families from Porto’s cramped workers’ housing. Building stopped after the first phase and resumed only in 2006, when the rows of white houses along the railway were finally completed.

title: Siza’s white museum in a park
episode: Álvaro Siza expands his Serralves Museum in Porto with angular gallery
description: Álvaro Siza opened the Serralves museum of contemporary art in 1999 in the grounds of a 1930s pink Art Deco villa. This short film shows the angular gallery he added more than 20 years later, when he was nearly 90.

title: How a hilly city built a metro
episode: How Porto somehow built a modern Metro
description: How Porto, a hilly mid-sized city, built Portugal’s second metro from 2002, reusing old railway lines, running trams on the surface, and tunneling under the old town. Trindade is the hub where most lines meet.

title: The team that stunned Europe in 2004
description: A short animated explainer on how José Mourinho’s FC Porto, a club outside Europe’s richest leagues, won the UEFA Cup in 2003 and the Champions League in 2004, and on the players who left for bigger clubs right after.

title: The bookshop with the crimson staircase
description: Livraria Lello, a bookshop opened in 1906, with carved wood, a stained-glass skylight, and a forked staircase painted red. Harry Potter fans made it famous, though J.K. Rowling has said she never visited it.

title: A concert hall cut like a gemstone
episode: Inside Casa da Música, Porto - With Backstage Access, Portugal
description: A walk through the Casa da Música, the concert hall by Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas that opened in 2005, a white concrete block faceted like a cut stone. The main hall has glass walls at both ends, so the audience can see the city.

title: A night of leeks, hammers, and fireworks
episode: 24 Hours at the Sao Joao Festival - Porto, Portugal
description: São João, Porto’s midsummer festival on the night of June 23, when crowds roam the old town tapping each other on the head with plastic hammers, grill sardines in the streets, and watch fireworks over the Douro at midnight.

title: Prince Henry and the first caravels
episode: Prince Henry of Portugal - Caravel Cruising and Exploration
description: A long, detailed talk by naval historian Drachinifel on Prince Henry “the Navigator” and the small, nimble ships, called caravels, that carried Portugal’s sailors down the coast of Africa. Henry is said to have been born in this house in 1394.
